headline: Chip Stocks Seize the Wheel as Semiconductors Pace a Broad Monday Rally
body_html:
Halfway through Monday's session, the tape is wearing a constructive shade of green. Advancing issues outnumber decliners by a ratio of roughly 345 to 197 across the 545-name universe, and the dominant theme is unmistakable: artificial-intelligence enthusiasm is pulling semiconductor names sharply higher, echoing reports that AI-linked stocks are lifting Wall Street broadly while Treasury yields ease and crude oil retreats.

Semiconductors lead every sector on the board with a gain of 2.42%, followed by Homebuilders at 1.11% and Software at 0.98%. The session's standout mover is Arm Holdings, whose shares have surged 15.02% intraday — by a wide margin the largest single-stock move in the universe today. Fellow chip-IP name Rambus is up 9.35%, AMD has added 8.86%, MaxLinear is ahead 8.72%, and Qualcomm has tacked on 7.49%, giving the sector a cohesive, conviction-driven tone rather than a one-off pop. Everpure rounds out the top gainers, up 7.87%, reflecting spillover enthusiasm into storage hardware.

The lone sector in the red is Energy, off 1.35%, consistent with the broader slide in oil prices. Into the close, watch whether the chip-sector bid holds its amplitude as the session matures, and monitor any developments from the ongoing diplomatic currents around the Middle East that could reprice crude into the final hour.

briefs.headline: Arm's Intraday Surge Commands the Session
briefs.body: Arm Holdings has rocketed 15.02% through midday, the single most dramatic move in the universe today. The gain appears tied to renewed investor confidence in AI-driven chip-architecture demand, with the broader semiconductor complex rallying in sympathy. The move gives the Semis-IP pocket a particularly sharp upward tilt heading into the afternoon.

briefs.headline: Novo Nordisk Leads Decliners as Healthcare Drags
briefs.body: Novo Nordisk has shed 7.83% in the sharpest selloff among decliners, dragging the broader Healthcare sector — which has managed only a 0.26% gain — away from the day's stronger performers. The move underscores divergence within defensives, even on a day when risk appetite is clearly elevated across growth-oriented pockets of the market.

briefs.headline: Oil's Drop Squeezes Energy Names as Geopolitical Picture Shifts
briefs.body: Energy is the lone sector in negative territory, falling 1.35% as crude prices retreat on a session where risk-asset enthusiasm dominates. Innovex International, an oil-services name, is among the session's notable decliners, off 3.72%. Reporting that the U.S. administration held back from pledging military support against Houthi forces appears to have tempered immediate supply-risk premiums in crude.

briefs.headline: Qatar Sovereign Fund and JP Morgan Plan $20 Billion Alliance
briefs.body: Qatar's sovereign wealth vehicle and JP Morgan Asset Management are set to formalize a $20 billion investment partnership, a move that signals continued appetite among Gulf capital pools for broad global asset deployment. The announcement adds a constructive macro backdrop to an already risk-on session and could have longer-term implications for institutional capital flows.

briefs.headline: Xi Arrives at Trump Summit as China Trade Data Impresses
briefs.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping opened a high-stakes summit with President Trump against a backdrop of strong Chinese trade momentum, according to reports. Markets are watching whether the meeting yields any softening of trade frictions; any positive signal could provide a further tailwind for globally exposed industrials and technology exporters in the back half of the session.

briefs.headline: Diesel Crunch Seen Stretching Well Into 2027
briefs.body: A deepening global diesel shortage, with storage tanks draining at an accelerating pace, is now expected to persist through at least 2027. The outlook compounds existing energy-market stress tied to Middle East supply-route concerns, and analysts warn that downstream industries reliant on diesel — from freight to construction — face a prolonged cost headwind that could weigh on margin forecasts across cyclical sectors.
